faq.q: Why does ice cream give you brain freeze?
faq.a: Very cold food touches the roof of your mouth, and blood vessels there narrow and then quickly widen. A face nerve sends a pain message, which you feel in your forehead.

faq.q: What happens to blood vessels in brain freeze?
faq.a: They squeeze narrow in the cold, then widen quickly to rush warm blood back. That quick change seems to trigger the ache.
asks: Why does cold make my head hurt?

faq.q: How do you stop brain freeze?
faq.a: Press your tongue against the roof of your mouth to warm it, and eat or drink cold things slowly.
asks: How do I get rid of brain freeze fast?

faq.a: No. It's a short, harmless ache that usually goes away in less than a minute. Your brain doesn't actually freeze.

faq.q: Why do I feel the pain in my forehead?
faq.a: The nerve that senses the cold also serves your forehead, so your brain gets mixed up about where the signal came from. This is called referred pain.

facts: The medical name for brain freeze is sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia.
Brain freeze is a kind of referred pain: felt in the forehead but triggered in the mouth.
